title: Rapid mixing of quantum spin chains at any finite temperature
abstract: We prove that a quasi-local quantum Gibbs sampler rapidly mixes to the Gibbs state of any 1D finite-range Hamiltonian at all finite temperatures in $\mathcal{O}\left(\log (n/\varepsilon)\right)$ time. Each update traces out a contiguous block of constant length and reconstructs it using the Petz recovery map, following early proposals for quantum heat-bath Gibbs samplers by Kastoryano and Brandão~\cite{kastoryano2016quantum}. Our proof directly bounds the distance between the updated state and the target Gibbs state using quantum Wasserstein distance of order $1$. We further provide $\mathcal{O}(\text{polylog}(n/\varepsilon))$ depth of quantum circuits to prepare these Gibbs states. We hope these techniques will facilitate the analysis and design of other Gibbs samplers.
summary: This paper proves that quantum Gibbs samplers rapidly mix to the true thermal Gibbs state for 1D quantum spin chains at any temperature. The mixing time scales logarithmically with system size, $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, and the required quantum circuit depth for state preparation is also polylogarithmic. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for simulating thermalization in quantum many-body physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the rapid mixing time of quantum Gibbs samplers for 1D quantum spin chains at any finite temperature.
main_result: Rapid mixing is proven for the quantum block heat-bath dynamics in $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$ time, and the Gibbs state preparation can be done with $O(	ext{polylog}(n/\epsilon))$ quantum circuit depth.
method: The analysis uses a path-coupling argument bounding the evolution in the quantum Wasserstein distance of order 1, combined with techniques for approximating quantum channels with efficient quantum circuits.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D quantum spin chain on a periodic lattice ($\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$) governed by a nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian. The dynamics are simulated using a quantum block heat-bath process defined by a Lindbladian.
key_observables: Mixing Time ($t_{	ext{mix}}$), Quantum Wasserstein distance ($W_1$), and Quantum Circuit Depth.
important_parameters: Finite temperature ($ eta$), system size ($n$), error tolerance ($\epsilon$), and constant block length ($\ell$).
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian is assumed to have bounded local interactions, and the proof relies on establishing specific boundary estimates and Lipschitz control conditions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 outlines the proof structure linking static properties to dynamical mixing. Table 1 compares the derived mixing time bound against other known results for spin systems.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the rapid mixing result using the quantum Wasserstein distance, followed by providing an explicit quantum circuit depth bound for state preparation. Later sections confirm the optimality of the logarithmic scaling for both periodic and open boundary conditions.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, resource-efficient theoretical guarantees for simulating thermalization dynamics in quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermalization and equilibrium states.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Proof outline of Theorem 1.1, read from right to left. The blue panel collects existing results on static properties of 1D Gibbs states [30, 61, 60], which prove Assumptions 4.3 and 4.4. Together, these imply the dynamical consequences shown in the orange panel: exponentially decaying exterior influence, exponential contraction in quantum W1 distance, and rapid mixing. The paper is intentionally organized in the reverse order.
